lastCheckpoint: Batch 26 CLOSED after two explicit user reconciliation passes: 26/26 scheduled journeys genuinely executed, 20 PASS, 1 FAILED_THEN_FIXED_PASS (V-003, a real row_version double-bump defect found via audit_log evidence, fixed, reran clean), 2 PRODUCT_GAP (AB-020, AB-039), 3 PARTIAL/tooling-limited (AB-030, AB-036, AB-037, individually traceable), 1 discovered journey (AB-043, PRODUCT_GAP_CONFIRMED, execution closed) executed same-run, 2 open Product Decisions (AB-020's reference_master gap, AB-043's loser-experience-consistency question which also covers AB-039, not double-counted)
notes: Batch 26 CLOSED 2026-09-28 after an explicit user-directed reconciliation pass corrected an earlier, premature closure. Full narrative in docs/journey-runs/BATCH_26_RESULTS.md. Reconciliation corrected: (1) AB-039 reclassified PASS -> PRODUCT_GAP_CONFIRMED: the concurrency-safety guarantee held (exactly one winner, no corruption) but the canonical journey's explicit expectation of a friendly 'already actioned' message for the loser was not met (loser got a silent, success-shaped idempotent response instead); AB-043 tracks the narrower mechanism separately so the finding is not duplicated. (2) AB-020 reclassified PRODUCT_DECISION_REQUIRED -> PRODUCT_GAP_CONFIRMED: reference_master genuinely has no maker-checker mechanism in current code, a confirmed gap against the canonical expectation, not merely an open question; the remediation choice (build the control vs amend the canonical expectation) remains a parked, unresolved Product Decision. (3) AB-025 redone: original route-level-only evidence (MANUAL UX VERIFIED) was ruled insufficient; redone with a genuine direct Server Action call as team_admin (captured a real Next.js Server Action HTTP request via an authorized user's real click, replayed it verbatim from team_admin's own real authenticated session against a fresh target, bypassing the page entirely) -> real 'You do not have permission to approve go_live' denial, zero mutation confirmed. (4) AB-027 redone: the cross-reference to AB-031 was ruled insufficient; redone as its own dedicated execution (a real, distinctly-permissioned checker directly calling the onboarding-case approve RPC against a genuinely out-of-scope record) -> real WORKFLOW_TEAM_REQUIRED denial, zero mutation/leakage confirmed via direct DB checks. (5) V-003 redone: the cross-reference to AB-039 was ruled insufficient; redone as a genuine 5-node-graph race (temporarily activated a real alternate workflow definition via the governed replace_active_workflow_definition RPC, restored the original afterward), verifying all six required assertions including the exact +2 row_version delta explained by source (two sequential customers UPDATE statements per single approval, not a race artifact) and honestly reporting the loser's silent-success behavior rather than smoothing it into a false PASS. (6) AB-030/036/037 split from one bundled residual line into three individually-traceable entries, each with its own exact unverified assertion. (7) V-002 finished from its already-staged real state (team membership already added) once the correct approve_customer_onboarding_case payload shape (customer_key/commercial_configuration_key/components, matching the RPC's own check constraints for pricing_rule_kind='flat', billing_quantity_basis, fx_snapshot_rate) was worked out via iterative real calls; genuine two-actor race confirmed exactly one Customer Master created, exactly one workflow transition. (8) V-004 executed fresh: created a disposable Commercial Configuration Version, used fn_resolve_workflow_next_approval directly to confirm which node was genuinely final for this request's segment routing before racing, confirmed exactly one commercial_components row activated despite two racing calls. AB-043 (discovered during AB-039, corrected during V-003 from an initial 'end node vs mid-graph' framing to the accurate 'was this approval the final one' framing, then independently re-confirmed via V-002 and V-004 in two more domains) is the single tracked entry for the cross-domain loser-experience Product Decision; AB-039 does not duplicate it. A second reconciliation pass (same day) investigated a reported V-003 row_version contradiction using real audit_log evidence (not source inspection alone): a single successful approve_customer_change_request call issued two sequential UPDATE statements against the customer row (one per-field update, one separate actor/timestamp stamp), and the table's own generic trg_customers_row_version trigger bumps row_version unconditionally on every UPDATE, so a 1-field change produced +2 (and an N-field change would have produced +(N+1)), breaking the canonical 'increments by exactly 1' invariant. Classified as a genuine defect (not intended dual-mutation, not fixture contamination, both ruled out with evidence). Bounded fix applied live (supabase/migrations/20261010000000_fix_approve_customer_change_request_row_version_double_bump.sql): consolidated the per-field UPDATEs and the actor stamp into exactly one UPDATE statement per approval. V-003 rerun fresh with a 2-field change specifically to prove the general case: row_version now increments by exactly 1 regardless of how many governed fields changed, confirmed via audit_log (exactly one UPDATE row, not two). V-003 reclassified FAILED THEN FIXED + PASS. AB-043 given an explicit terminal status (PRODUCT_GAP_CONFIRMED, execution closed, one Product Decision still open, not double-counted against AB-039). V-004 re-inspected assertion-by-assertion against existing evidence (previously-active-version supersession and no-duplicate-activation confirmed via direct query; fx_snapshot_rate correctly null for same-currency but not deeply exercised with a real cross-currency value, disclosed honestly); remained PASS with no rerun needed. No CI-level regression test exists for the row_version fix: this repo's test suite is unit-level only (mocked Supabase client), with no live-database integration-test harness for Postgres RPC invariants; the live rerun stands in as verification, and adding such a harness is flagged as a legitimate follow-up, not built here. Supabase CLI (`supabase db push`) was unavailable in this environment (no stored access token, no interactive login); the migration file was written with the correct content and timestamp for the historical record, and the equivalent CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION was applied directly against the live dev database via the already-authorized MCP connection; a future `supabase db push` will safely re-apply the same (idempotent) definition once CLI auth is available, at which point it will also be correctly registered in the tracked migration history. tsc --noEmit exits 0. npx vitest run: 111 test files, 1046 tests, all passing (rerun after the fix). Do not start Batch 27.
